name: tags: token match inside a skill, then skills.true appended
why: Spec §1: "A skill string s 'matches a cluster' ... when any spelling matches inside s as a whole token". 'Stakeholder management' contains the whole token 'stakeholder' (case-insensitive), so f1 matches; the skills.true item is appended after all facts as ["skills.true", item].

name: tags: plural spelling does not match singular skill
why: Spec §1 + matching rule: 'Stakeholders' equals the spelling ignoring case and surrounding spaces, so it matches; 'Stakeholder' is neither equal to 'stakeholders' nor contains it as a whole token (the trailing 's' breaks the match), so it does not match.

name: tags: fact with resume_ok false is excluded, skills.true still included
why: Spec §1: "Every skill of a fact with resume_ok not false ... then every skills.true item ... that matches". f1 has resume_ok false so its matching skill is skipped; the skills.true item still matches and is returned.

name: tags: entry with on_resume false is excluded
why: Spec §1: fact skills count only when "whose entry has on_resume not false". e1 has on_resume false, so 'Stakeholder management' is excluded and there are no skills.true matches.

name: tags: skills.true groups in group order, non-matching items skipped
why: Spec §1: skills.true items come "groups in their order". Group 'lead' yields 'Stakeholder engagement' (skip 'Team leadership'), group 'ops' yields 'Stakeholder ops' (skip 'Budgeting'), group 'gov' yields 'Stakeholder governance'. skills.not_true is never used.

name: gaps: term dropped when the page already contains its jd_spelling
why: hits('python')=1 ('Python' token); in_title=false; score=3×min(1,3)×1=3; jd_spelling='python'; term is true (f1 skill 'Python' matches). Spec §2: keep only when "(b) the page does not contain its jd_spelling" — page has 'Python', so it is dropped.
title: Backend Engineer

name: gaps: another spelling on the page gives state other_spelling
why: Spec: 'stakeholder' does not match inside 'stakeholders' (adjacent letters break the match), so hits: stakeholder 0 + stakeholders 1 = 1. jd_spelling is the spelling with most matches = 'stakeholders'. score=2×min(1,3)×1=2. Term is true (f1 'Stakeholder management' has token 'stakeholder'). page contains 'stakeholder', a different spelling → state = "other_spelling".
title: Product Manager

name: gaps: term that is not "true" is dropped
why: hits('python')=1, score=3×1×1=3, jd_spelling='python', page empty. But spec §2 keeps a term only when "(a) it is 'true': a fact as in §1 has a matching skill, or a skills.true item matches" — no fact skill or skills.true item matches 'python' (only 'Java' exists), so the term is dropped.
title: Engineer

name: gaps: title match doubles the score
why: hits('python')=2; in_title=true ('Python' is a token of the title) so multiplier 2; score=2×min(2,3)×2=8 (rounded 4dp → 8). page is empty → state 'missing'. facts lists all matching facts in fact order: f1 then f2.
title: Python Engineer

name: gaps: hits are capped at 3
why: Spec: "score = weight × min(hits, 3)". hits('sql')=5, min(5,3)=3; in_title=false; score=1×3×1=3. jd_spelling='sql', page empty → state 'missing'.
title: Data Analyst

name: gaps: LLMOps does not match the LLM spelling
why: Spec matching rule: "letters / digits / '&' / '+' next to it break the match: 'LLM' does not match 'LLMOps'". hits('LLM')=0, so the cluster is "skipped" by jd_terms and produces no item even though a fact skill 'LLM' would make the term true.
title: ML Engineer

name: gaps: n cuts the sorted list
why: Each term hits once, none in title: alpha=3×1×1=3, beta=2×1×1=2, gamma=1×1×1=1. Sorted score desc → alpha, beta, gamma; first n=2 keeps alpha and beta only. All are true (f1 has matching skills) and the page is empty.
title: Generalist

name: aggregate: tie on score and jds broken by term asc
why: Both terms appear in 1 of 1 JD: share=1/1=1.0, score 3 each (sum of a single score). Rows sorted "score desc, then jds desc, then term asc" → alpha before beta.

name: aggregate: share rounding to 4 decimals
why: python appears in 2 of 3 lists: share=2/3=0.666666… rounded 0.6667, score=2+2=4, spellings {python:2}, states missing 1 + other_spelling 1. go appears in 1 of 3: share=1/3=0.3333, score=1. Sorted score desc → python, go.

name: aggregate: n_jds 0 gives share 0
why: Spec §3: "share = jds / n_jds rounded to 4 decimals (0 when n_jds is 0)". The term appears in 1 list, so jds=1, but n_jds=0 forces share=0; score stays 3 and counts stay as observed.

name: aggregate: spellings/states counts and sorted fact union
why: Term appears in both lists: jds=2, share=2/2=1.0, score=2+2=4. spellings counts jd_spelling per list {'stakeholders':1,'stakeholder':1}; states {'missing':1,'other_spelling':1}; facts = sorted union of ['f2','f1'] and ['f1','f3'] = ['f1','f2','f3'].

name: deny: remove matching skills from one fact
why: Spec §4: "fact_id = a fact id: that fact's skills that match the cluster are removed (others kept, order kept); returns the removed ones in order". 'Stakeholder management' matches; 'Python' and 'SQL' are kept in order.

name: deny: skills.true removes from every group
why: Spec §4: "fact_id = 'skills.true': the same for every skills.true group". Group a loses 'Stakeholder engagement' (keeps 'Python'), group b loses 'Team stakeholders' (empty left); removed returned in group order then item order.

name: deny: nothing matching leaves everything unchanged
why: Spec §4: "An unknown id or nothing matching → [] and nothing changes". No skill of f1 contains a whole token 'stakeholder'/'stakeholders', so [] is returned and f1 keeps both skills.

name: deny: other facts are never touched
why: Spec §4: "Other facts are never touched". Denying f1 removes only its 'Stakeholder management'; f2 keeps its matching skill 'Stakeholder engagement' untouched.

name: candidates: valid candidate with gap resolved through a synonym
why: Spec §5: gap 'LLMs' equals a synonym of role keyword term 'LLM', so the cluster is {LLM, LLMs, large language models}; 'LLM' is a whole token of the text → matches. e1 is on the master, text is not an existing bullet/reserve text exactly → no kinds.

name: candidates: entry_not_on_master
why: Spec §5 first rule: "entry_not_on_master — its entry_id is not an entry_id of the master". e7 is not in master. The text contains 'stakeholders' so no_gap_term does not fire, and it is not equal to any master text so not_new does not fire.

name: candidates: not_new against a reserve text
why: Spec §5 second rule: "not_new — its text equals an existing master bullet or reserve text exactly". Text equals the reserve text. gap 'junior' equals no role keyword term/synonym, so the cluster is just 'junior', which matches the text as a token → no_gap_term does not fire.

name: candidates: empty gap gives no_gap_term
why: Spec §5 third rule: "no_gap_term — gap is empty ...". gap is "" so the rule fires; entry e1 exists and the text is not an exact master bullet/reserve text, so only no_gap_term is reported.

name: candidates: gap cluster via synonym matches; unrelated text triggers no_gap_term
why: Candidate 1: gap 'LLM' equals the term, so the cluster includes synonym 'large language models', present as whole tokens in the text → matches, entry and newness fine → no kinds. Candidate 2: gap 'LLMs' cluster is {LLM, LLMs, large language models}; 'Shipped retrieval pipelines' contains none → no_gap_term.

name: bank: insert at end of a middle section
why: Spec §6: find '## Alpha', insert after its last non-empty line ('alpha two') before the next '## ' line, "keeping the blank line(s) that follow" (one blank line kept before '## Beta'); result ends with exactly one newline.
bank:
# Bank

## Alpha
alpha one
alpha two

## Beta
beta one
heading: Alpha
expect:
# Bank

## Alpha
alpha one
alpha two
new bullet

## Beta
beta one

name: bank: insert at end of the last section
why: Spec §6: last non-empty line before "the end" is 'beta one'; the new line goes right after it, and the result ends with exactly one newline.
bank:
## Alpha
alpha one

## Beta
beta one
heading: Beta
expect:
## Alpha
alpha one

## Beta
beta one
beta two

name: bank: missing heading appends a new section
why:
Spec §6: "No such heading → append '

## heading
' + the lines at the end". Input stripped of trailing newlines is '# Bank

## Alpha
alpha one', then '

## Gamma
' + 'gamma one' + final newline.
heading: Gamma
expect:
# Bank

## Alpha
alpha one

## Gamma
gamma one

name: bank: blank lines after the last non-empty line are kept
why: Spec §6: insertion goes "right after its last non-empty line ... keeping the blank line(s) that follow". The two blank lines before '## Beta' stay after the inserted line.
bank:
## Alpha
alpha one


## Beta
beta one
heading: Alpha
expect:
## Alpha
alpha one
new


## Beta
beta one

name: bank: trailing newlines stripped, result ends with exactly one newline
why: Spec §6: "The result always ends with exactly one '\n' (trailing newlines of the input are stripped first)". After stripping, 'alpha one' is the last non-empty line; 'x' is inserted and a single final newline is emitted.
heading: Alpha
